newsitem.title: DUBAI: Strong earthquake hits northeastern Iran.
newsitem.headline: Strong earthquake hits northeastern Iran.

text.p: A strong earthquake measuring 7.1 on the Richter scale hit Mashhad and other cities in Iran's northeastern Khorasan province on Saturday, the official Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
It said the quake hit the southeast of the province at 12:28 p.m. (0758 GMT). The agency said no reports of damage or casualties were available yet.

Radio Tehran said the quake was felt in three adjoining provinces. Iran television monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation said the headquarters of the natural disaster relief services had been placed on full alert.
The cities of Qaem and Birjand were also hit by the quake, IRNA said.
Earthquakes stronger than force six can cause widespread damage.
Quakes hit Iran regularly. The worst recorded one, measuring 7.3 on the Richter scale, killed 35,000 people in a densely populated area near the Caspian sea coast in 1990.
A minor earthquake measuring 3.6 hit the southern Iranian city of Larestan on Friday. IRNA said that was the third to hit southern Iran in less than one month.
In Early February, two earthquakes measuring 6.1 and 5.4 on the Richter scale killed at least 79 people and injured 260 in a mountainous region in northeastern Iran.
At least 1,000 people were killed and more than 36,000 made homeless when a quake measuring 5.5 on the Richter scale hit northwest Iran on February 28.
